**VERDICT: ACCEPT-WITH-RESERVATIONS** **Overall Assessment**: The component demonstrates strong accessibility design decisions, particularly around persistent live regions, focus management, and reduced-motion handling. However, two semantic structure gaps remain: a redundant ARIA role on the list element that violates WCAG 4.1.2, and a lack of tabular semantics for financial data that degrades screen reader parsing. These are fixable design refinements rather than blocking failures. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: 1. Redundant `role="list"` on `
    ` (WCAG 4.1.2 violation) 2. Financial row data lacking column context for AT (WCAG 1.3.1) 3. Potential double-announcement or focus shift on state change 4. Color contrast verification needed for error/status text *Actual findings aligned with predictions 1 & 2. Prediction 3 was mitigated by the persistent DOM design. Prediction 4 passed verification.* **Critical Findings** (blocks access): None. The component implements core interaction patterns correctly and does not block access for any assistive technology user group. **Major Findings** (significantly degrades experience): 1. **Redundant `role="list"` on `

        ` - User Group: Screen reader users (older AT versions, JAWS/NVDA legacy modes) - WCAG/APG Citation: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value — "Do not use ARIA roles when equivalent native HTML semantics are available." - Why this matters: `
          ` already has an implicit `role="list"`. Explicitly adding it is redundant and can cause older assistive technologies to double-process the list or ignore it entirely, breaking list navigation. - Fix: Remove `role="list"`. Let native HTML semantics handle the role. If custom styling requires a wrapper, keep `
            ` for the list container and use `
            ` for any outer wrappers. 2. **Financial transaction data lacks tabular semantics** - Evidence: Lines 30-34: `
          • {t.payee}{t.amount}
            • ` - User Group: Screen reader users, cognitive accessibility users - WCAG/APG Citation: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships — "Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text." WAI-ARIA APG recommends tables for tabular data. - Why this matters: Screen readers will announce payee and amount sequentially without column context. Users cannot easily parse which value corresponds to which attribute. Financial data is inherently tabular; linear list semantics obscure the relationship. - Fix: Convert to a `` with `` and ``, or use a definition list (`
            `) with `
            {t.payee}
            {t.amount}
            `. If keeping flexbox/list, add `aria-label` to each row describing the relationship (e.g., `aria-label={\`${t.payee}: ${t.amount}\`}`) or use `role="row"` with `aria-rowindex` and column roles. **Minor Findings** (friction but workaround exists): - **`aria-atomic="true"` on polite status region**: Line 18: `
            `. While valid, `aria-atomic="true"` forces screen readers to re-read the entire region content on every update. If only the transaction count changes, this creates unnecessary cognitive load. Consider removing `aria-atomic` so AT announces only the changed text, or keep it if partial updates are rare and full context is preferred. - **Persistent empty alert region**: Line 24: `
            ` remains in DOM when `status !== 'error'`. While most modern ATs ignore empty `role="alert"` elements, it's cleaner to conditionally render or apply `aria-hidden="true"` when empty to prevent any edge-case announcements. **Enhancements** (best practice not met): - **Button disabled state during async**: The comment notes the parent owns request lifecycle. If the retry button isn't visually/programmatically disabled (`aria-disabled="true"`) during loading, double-submit is a UX risk. While not strictly an AT design gap, adding `aria-disabled={status === 'loading'}` improves cognitive clarity and prevents redundant announcements. - **Focus indicator contrast verification**: CSS uses `#0b5fff` for focus outline on white background (~4.6:1). This passes WCAG 2.4.13 (3:1 threshold), but verify against all supported backgrounds. If dark mode is added, ensure the focus color adapts or uses a contrasting fallback. **What's Missing** (gaps, unhandled edge cases, unstated assumptions): - **Table/Definition List conversion**: No semantic mapping for payee/amount relationship. Financial data benefits from explicit column headers or definition structure. - **`aria-disabled` on retry during async**: Assumed parent handles it, but component doesn't expose programmatic disabled state for AT consistency. - **Empty-state alert handling**: Persistent `role="alert"` without conditional visibility or `aria-hidden` when empty. **Multi-Perspective Notes**: - **Screen reader user**: Logical heading/landmark structure. Status/alert regions announce correctly due to persistent DOM pattern. Transaction list is announced linearly without column context, making financial data harder to parse. Redundant `role="list"` may confuse legacy AT. - **Keyboard-only user**: Tab order is logical. Focus indicator meets 2.4.13 requirements. No traps or unexpected focus shifts. Button remains in DOM during state changes, preserving focus position. - **Low vision user (200% zoom, high contrast)**: Focus outline uses `outline-offset: 2px` and 3px width, meeting 2.4.13 perimeter/contrast requirements. Color contrast for error (`#b42318`) and button (`#0b5fff`) passes AA text thresholds on white. No horizontal scroll or reflow issues in the component structure. - **Cognitive accessibility**: Error message explicitly names the recovery action ("Select Retry"). Loading state is clear. States are mutually exclusive and persistent, reducing cognitive load from mounting/unmounting regions. Financial data parsing remains the primary friction point without tabular semantics. **Verdict Justification**: The component's live region strategy, focus management, and reduced-motion handling are design strengths that align with WAI-ARIA APG patterns for dynamic content. The two major findings (redundant role, missing tabular semantics) significantly impact screen reader parsing but do not block core functionality. Removing `role="list"` and adopting table/definition list semantics for financial data will elevate the component to a fully accessible design. Verdict upgraded from REJECT to ACCEPT-WITH-RESERVATIONS because fixes are straightforward and don't require architectural changes. **Open Questions (unscored)**: - Does the parent component conditionally render this panel, or does it mount once?
